# Capacitor (web app shipped as an iOS and Android app)

These rules add to the core build skills of the quality pack.

## Rules

- The shipped app loads its bundled files: server.url is for development only. A bare wrapper around a live site is refused by Apple (guideline 4.2).
- Bring what a site cannot: notifications, offline, native share, camera or biometrics depending on the product.
- server.allowNavigation limited to the app's origins, never "*"; cleartext off. The native bridge is exposed to every page loaded in the WebView.
- Session tokens in native secure storage (Keychain, Keystore) through a plugin, never in localStorage or Preferences.
- Safe areas: viewport-fit=cover and env(safe-area-inset-*) on fixed bars; height in dvh, not 100vh.
- Keyboard: Keyboard plugin set so the field and the main action stay visible; fields at 16 px or more.
- Android back button handled (App.addListener('backButton')): it returns to the previous screen and only closes the app from home.
- No hover as the only way to act; touch feedback under 100 ms; no 300 ms delay (touch-action: manipulation).
- Run `npx cap sync` after any plugin change and commit the android/ and ios/ folders.
- The same key tasks are played in the browser (qp flows) and on a device (qp mobile flows).

## Check commands

Used by `/qp:audit`. `{pm}` is the project's package manager, `{url}` the app URL, `{host}` its host name.

| Check | Command | Passes if |
| --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | `{pm} exec tsc --noEmit` | exit code 0 |
| lint | `{pm} run lint` | exit code 0, no errors |
| test_run | `{pm} test` | exit code 0 |
| deps_audit | `{pm} audit --audit-level=high` | no high or critical advisory; then `npx cap doctor` reports matching versions |
| license_check | `npx --yes license-checker-rseidelsohn --summary --failOn 'GPL;AGPL'` | exit code 0 |
